ἄνθρωπος ὁ ὑπὲρ ἄλλων δεόμενος, οὐκ ἄλλως ἀκούεται, εἰ μὴ ἐκεῖνος ἔργῳ δείξῃ
τὴν μετάνοιαν. οὕτω γὰρ ἡ δέησις ἰσχύει τοῦ δικαίου ἐνεργουμένη διὰ τοῦ
1
ἁμαρτήσαντος. ἵνα οὖν εἰς πέρας ἀχθῇ τὸ πρᾶγμα, δεῖ ἀμ φότερα συνδραμεῖν, καὶ τὴν
τοῦ δικαίου εὐχὴν καὶ τὸ ἔργον τοῦ μετανοοῦντος.} 6 Ὁ μὲν Ἠσαῦ «πυρράκης ἦν
ὡσεὶ δορὰ δασύς», τὴν ἐξ ἁμαρτίας ἔχων νεκρότητα καὶ φονῶν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰακώβ. ὁ δὲ
∆αβὶδ πυρράκης ἦν μετὰ κάλλους ὀφθαλμῶν , ἵνα τὸ διορατικὸν δηλώσῃ τοῦ ∆αβίδ.
7 Πῶς ἀνήρ , καὶ πῶς συνετὸς ἐν λόγῳ , πῶς δὲ καὶ πολε μιστὴς ὁ ἔτι πρόβατα
ποιμαίνων; οὐκ ἄρα ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ ἐλάλησεν εἰπών, ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐσόμενα προειπὼν ὡς
παρόντα, καὶ μαρτυρεῖ τῷ ∆αβὶδ ἅπερ ἔμελλεν εἶναι, πλὴν τοῦ κύριος μετ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ
τε ἀγαθὸς τῷ εἴδει , ἅπερ ἐκ παιδικῆς ἡλικίας προσῆν αὐτῷ καὶ παρέμενε, τὸ μὲν
φύσει, τὸ δὲ χάριτι. 8 Ἐπειδὴ δυνατὸς ἦν ὁ Σαοὺλ πλῆθος ἔχων βοηθοῦν αὐτῷ κακῶς
κατὰ τοῦ ∆αβίδ, οἱ δὲ δύο μόνοι ἐδιώκοντο ὁ Σαμουὴλ καὶ ὁ ∆αβίδ, ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ χάρις
ποιεῖ προφητεύειν τὸν Σαοὺλ οὐ μόνον ὅσα κατ' αὐτοῦ ἦν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ὑπὲρ τοῦ
∆αβίδ, καὶ ῥίπτει γυμνόν , προσημαίνουσα ὅτι γυμνωθήσεται τῆς βασιλείας. 9
Βεβήλους λέγει νῦν οὐ τοὺς ἀκαθάρτους, ἀλλὰ τοὺς οὐχ ἁγίους, πρὸς ἀντιδιαστολὴν
τῶν ἁγίων ἄρτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης παρα τιθεμένων. ἓξ γὰρ εἶχεν ἄρτους ἡ
τράπεζα διαπαντὸς ἀλλασσομένους ὑπὲρ τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, οὓς
ἐνωπίους ἐκάλουν, ὡς εἶναι ἕκαστον τῶν ἄρτων ὑπὲρ δύο φυλῶν προσφερόμενον,
τοὺς δὲ ἓξ ὑπὲρ τῶν δώδεκα φυλῶν. τί οὖν ἐκ τούτου καλὸν ἐγίνετο; τὰς φυλὰς τοῦ
Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ὁμόνοιαν συνάπτεσθαι. τί δὲ κρεῖττον προε σημαίνετο; τοὺς μακαρίους
ἀποστόλους ἀνὰ δύο δύο πέμπεσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος τὰ πρῶτα κηρύττειν ἐν ταῖς
φυλαῖς τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ὡς εἶναι ἓξ ἅμα τῶν δώδεκα μαθητῶν τὸν ἀριθμόν. {Ἄρτος
λαϊκὸς οὐχ ὅτι οἱ μὴ ἅγιοι βέβηλοι, ἀλλ' ὅτι πρὸς τὸ ἅγιον συγκρινόμενοι.} 10
Σήμερον ἁγιασθήσεται διὰ τὰ σκεύη ἀσαφέστερον μὲν εἶπε, σημαίνει δὲ τοῦτο. τὰ μὲν
παιδία μου ἡγίασται καὶ ἀπέσχηται γυναικὸς καὶ χθὲς καὶ τρίτην ἡμέραν · τοῦτο γὰρ
τὸ φάναι αὐ τὸν καὶ τὰ παιδία ἡγνισμένα . εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἦν, πάντως ἡγιάζετο διὰ τοῦ
φαγεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῆς προθέσεως. πεισθεὶς ὁ ἱερεὺς τοῖς εἰρη μένοις δίδωσι τῷ ∆αβὶδ
τῶν ἄρτων, οὓς οὐκ ἐχρῆν ἑτέρους φαγεῖν ἢ μόνους τοὺς ἱερέας. τοῦτο δὲ τῆς
προφητείας ἐστὶ τῆς δι' ἔργων δηλούσης, ὅτι μήποτε ἄλλης οὔσης τῆς βασιλικῆς
φυλῆς, τουτέστι τῆς Ἰούδα, καὶ ἄλλης τῆς ἱερατικῆς φυλῆς, λέγω δὴ <τῆς>
Λευιτικῆς, ἔμελλον συνάπτεσθαι καὶ ἓν ἀποτελεῖσθαι τό τε ἱερατικὸν ἀξίωμα καὶ τὸ
<βασιλικὸν> ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ ἐκ ∆αβὶδ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἱερέως τε ὁμοῦ καὶ
βασιλέως, τοῦ «κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ». 11 Τὸν Νεεσσάρ · δηλοῖ ἢ ὅτι δι'
ἁμαρτίας παρέμενε ∆ωὴκ ὁ Ἰδουμαῖος ἐνώπιον κυρίου θεραπευόμενος καὶ
ἐξομολογούμενος, ἢ δαιμονῶν ὡς ὁ Σαούλ , οὗ τὰς ἡμιόνους ἔβοσκεν. 12 Ὁ Σαοὺλ
τοῦ πονηροῦ πνεύματος τύπον φέρει, ἄρξαντος τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ τότε εἰπόντος· οὐκ
ἔχομεν βασιλέα. καὶ γὰρ ὁ πάλαι λαὸς ἐξουδενώσας τὸν κύριον βασιλεύοντα αὐτοῦ,
ᾔτησε τὸν Σαοὺλ ἄρ χοντα αὐτῷ δοθῆναι. 13 Οὐκ οὐρεῖ τις ἑστὼς καὶ τοῦτο πρὸς
τοῖχον , ἐὰν μὴ σχολάζῃ τοῦτο οὖν λέγει καὶ τὸν ἀμέριμνον καὶ μηδὲν προσδοκῶντα
pass_a_gloss: person who petitions for others is not otherwise heard unless that one shows repentance in deed. For so the righteous person's petition has force when energized through the one who sinned. Therefore for the matter to be brought to an end both must run together: the righteous one's prayer and the repenting one's work. Esau was reddish like a hairy skin, having the deadness from sin and murderous against Jacob; but David was reddish with beauty of eyes, to show David's clear-sightedness. How a man, and how understanding in speech, and how also a warrior, the one still shepherding sheep? Therefore he did not speak from himself when he spoke, but foretelling the things to be as present, and he witnesses to David what was about to be, except "the Lord is with him" and "good in appearance," which were present to him from childhood and remained, the one by nature, the other by grace. Since Saul was powerful having a multitude helping him badly against David, and only the two were pursued—Samuel and David—God's grace makes Saul prophesy not only what was against him but also what was for David, and casts him naked, foresignifying that he will be stripped of the kingdom. He now calls "profane" not the unclean but those not holy, in distinction from the holy loaves set on the table. For the table had six loaves continually changed for the twelve tribes of Israel, which they called shewbread, so that each loaf was offered for two tribes, and the six for the twelve. What good came from this? Binding the tribes of Israel toward concord. What better was foresignified? The blessed apostles being sent two by two by the Savior to preach first in Israel's tribes, so that six at once make the number of the twelve disciples. Lay bread is not that the non-holy are profane, but that compared with the holy. "Today it will be sanctified through the vessels" he said more unclearly, but it means this: my children have been sanctified and have kept from a woman both yesterday and the third day—for that is his saying that the children also are purified. And if not, he was wholly sanctified through eating the bread of the presentation. Persuaded by what was said the priest gives David of the loaves which none else ought to eat but only the priests. This belongs to prophecy shown through deeds: that though the royal tribe was one—Judah—and the priestly another—Levi—they were about to be joined and made one, the priestly dignity and the royal, in the presence of our Savior from David, priest and king together, "according to the order of Melchizedek." Neessar: it shows either that through sin Doeg the Idumaean remained before the Lord being healed and confessing, or demonized like Saul, whose mules he pastured. Saul bears the type of the evil spirit that ruled Israel then saying, We have no king; for the ancient people, having despised the Lord reigning over them, asked that Saul be given them as ruler. No one urinates standing even toward a wall unless he is at leisure; this then he says also of the carefree and expecting nothing
pass_b_english: …person who petitions for others is not heard unless the one prayed for shows repentance in deed. The righteous person's plea has force when it is energized through the sinner. For the matter to reach its end, both must run together: the righteous one's prayer and the repenting one's work.

Esau was reddish like a hairy hide, carrying deadness from sin and murderous toward Jacob; David was reddish with beauty of eyes, to show his clear sight. How then is the still-shepherding lad called a man, understanding in speech, and a warrior? The speaker did not speak from himself, but foretold what would be as if present, witnessing what David was about to become—except "[[the Lord is with him >> Bible:1 Samuel 16:18]]" and "good in appearance," which were his from childhood, one by nature and one by grace.

Saul had strength and a crowd helping him wickedly against David, while only Samuel and David were hunted. God's grace makes Saul prophesy not only what cuts against himself but what favors David, and casts him down naked, foresignifying that he will be stripped of the kingdom.

"Profane" here means not the unclean but those who are not holy, set over against the holy loaves of the table. The table held six loaves continually changed for Israel's twelve tribes—called shewbread—so each loaf stood for two tribes and the six for twelve. The good of this was binding the tribes toward concord; the better foresign was the apostles sent two by two by the Savior to preach first among Israel's tribes, so that six pairs make twelve disciples. Lay bread is "profane" only by comparison with the holy, not because the non-holy are unclean as such.

"Today it will be sanctified through the vessels" is said less clearly, but means: my children have been sanctified and kept from a woman yesterday and the day before—that is his claim that the children also are purified. If not, he was sanctified through eating the bread of the Presence. Persuaded, the priest gives David loaves none else ought to eat but priests. This is prophecy through deeds: the royal tribe (Judah) and the priestly (Levi) were about to be joined into one dignity—priestly and royal—in our Savior from David, priest and king together "[[according to the order of Melchizedek >> Bible:Psalm 110:4]]."

Neessar shows either that through sin Doeg the Idumaean remained before the Lord being treated and confessing, or that he was demonized like Saul, whose mules he pastured. Saul bears the type of the evil spirit that once ruled Israel when they said they had no king: the ancient people, despising the Lord who reigned over them, asked that Saul be given as ruler.
No one stands and urinates even toward a wall unless he is at leisure; so he speaks also of the carefree person who expects nothing…

choices.choice: Six loaves / twelve tribes → apostles two by two; kept without adding claims.
